nodes.label: Chromium Port Blockers
nodes.rationale: Chromium blocked on: multiprocess sandbox (seccomp-bpf/namespaces), GPU EGL/GBM/DRM or ANGLE/Vulkan path, V8 JIT (jitless possible but milestone-sized), GN build integration (35M LOC). Ozone/Wayland and C++ runtime blockers were resolved by M49 and M55 respectively.

nodes.label: V8 as Remaining Engine Blocker for Chromium
nodes.rationale: After M55 C++ runtime and M49 Wayland compositor, remaining hard blockers for Chromium are: V8 (jitless is milestone-sized port), real GPU path (EGL/GBM M59), sandbox (seccomp/namespaces M63), and 35M-LOC GN/Ninja build.
nodes.norm_label: v8 as remaining engine blocker for chromium

nodes.label: Arch-Guard Stamp Fix for Initramfs
nodes.rationale: native_smoke linked without libc/crt0 so its only prerequisite was the source file, surviving an ARCH switch. Fix: arch-guard stamp userspace/build/.arch wipes userspace/build on arch change so every output relinks. Prevents stale cross-arch ELF in initramfs.

nodes.label: GN Build System Port as Dominant V8 Blocker
nodes.rationale: Adding b1nix as a GN target requires editing //build/config, toolchain defs, v8_target_os plumbing, and platform-*.cc. Not a flag but a from-scratch port. Same shape as M61 Chromium but scoped to V8. Estimated weeks of GN plumbing before a single V8 object file compiles.
nodes.norm_label: gn build system port as dominant v8 blocker

nodes.label: madvise/MAP_NORESERVE as V8 Runtime Blocker
nodes.rationale: V8 OS::DiscardSystemPages, OS::DecommitPages, and the page allocator use madvise(MADV_FREE/DONTNEED) and MAP_NORESERVE. Missing from b1nix at probe time. Stubbing as no-ops is functionally possible at memory-efficiency cost. This was the #1 runtime blocker.

nodes.label: Duktape as Pragmatic V8 Alternative
nodes.rationale: Duktape already compiled into NetSurf. Exposing as /bin/js is 1-2 day task delivering a working JS REPL. V8 jitless buys ECMAScript-2023 conformance and speed, not JS execution capability.

nodes.norm_label: m46 vfs integrity and posix process conformance audit

nodes.label: V1 ext4/ext2 Block Allocator Race (CRITICAL)
nodes.rationale: ext4_alloc_block_tx and ext2_alloc_*_tx performed unsynchronized RMW on on-disk bitmaps. Two CPUs could allocate the same block. Fix: per-fs sleeping mutex alloc_lock across all 8 allocator entry points.

nodes.label: V4 Shared FD Table Lifecycle UAF (HIGH)
nodes.rationale: scheduler_exit_current unconditionally freed fd_table even with CLONE_FILES siblings alive. Fix: fdtable_release mirrors mm_release_user, last user frees under g_mm_release_lock.
nodes.norm_label: v4 shared fd table lifecycle uaf (high)

nodes.label: R3-3 mqueue Handle as Raw Kernel Pointer (CRITICAL security)
nodes.rationale: SYS_MQ_OPEN returned kernel VA of queue struct as handle. SYS_MQ_SEND/RECEIVE cast it back with zero validation enabling arbitrary kernel memory write (256 bytes) from any process. Fix: return validated table index, never raw pointer.
nodes.norm_label: r3-3 mqueue handle as raw kernel pointer (critical security)

nodes.label: R3-4 ext4 Uninitialized Extent High Bit Bug (CRITICAL)
nodes.rationale: ext4_extent_lookup and ext4_add_extent compared raw ee_len without masking the uninitialized-extent flag bit (>0x8000). Mounting real ext4 with fallocate extents caused cross-file reads/writes. Fix: ext4_extent_len() accessor used at all three sites.
nodes.norm_label: r3-4 ext4 uninitialized extent high bit bug (critical)

nodes.label: V8 vfs_mount Slot Claim Without Lock (MEDIUM)
nodes.rationale: Free-slot scan and pre-registration ran without vfs_mount_lock. Two concurrent mounts could claim one slot. Fix: slot claim + field init and post-mount finalization now under vfs_mount_lock; sleeping fs->mount() callback stays outside.
nodes.norm_label: v8 vfs_mount slot claim without lock (medium)

nodes.label: P1 Exit Status Signal-Death Misreporting (HIGH)
nodes.rationale: Kernel stored one int exit_code for both normal exits and signal deaths. exit(139) was reported as WIFSIGNALED/SIGSEGV. Fix: signal deaths tagged with TASK_EXIT_SIGNALED bit 16; waitpid encodes from flag not range.

nodes.label: R4-4 ELF Loader e_phentsize Not Validated (HIGH)
nodes.rationale: user_load_elf64 and user_load_elf32 never checked e_phentsize equals sizeof(elf64_phdr)/elf32_phdr. Small/zero e_phentsize caused OOB heap reads; e_phoff overflow bypassed the size check. Fix: reject wrong e_phentsize; use subtraction-form bounds.
nodes.norm_label: r4-4 elf loader e_phentsize not validated (high)

nodes.label: wl_shm Kept Native in displayd (not libwayland-server)
nodes.rationale: wl_shm lives in displayd not ported libwayland-server because: (1) b1nix has no SIGBUS-on-beyond-EOF semantics that upstream wl_shm's crash-guard relies on; (2) wayland-shm.c is not compiled into libwayland-server.a and adopting it pulls in the full 2400-LOC object model rewrite.
nodes.norm_label: wl_shm kept native in displayd (not libwayland-server)

nodes.label: Hand-Rolled Wayland Wire Marshalling Design
nodes.rationale: wayland-scanner codegen only emits the wl_resource/listener model requiring full libwayland-server runtime. Cost: ~9200 generated LOC + codegen build step + vendored protocol XML + libwayland-server.a link for zero functional gain. Hand-rolled dispatch keeps server one tiny file.

nodes.label: zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1 Honestly Rejected (no GEM path)
nodes.rationale: zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1 is advertised but create() replies failed and create_immed() is dropped because b1nix has no GEM/dmabuf importer. GPU buffers reach host via /dev/virtio-gpu outside Wayland. Conforming client falls back to SHM.

nodes.label: Higher-Half Kernel VA Layout
nodes.rationale: Both kernels linked at higher-half VA (x86_64 at 0xFFFFFFFF80000000; i686 at 0x80000000) so a large kernel image with embedded Mesa initramfs no longer overlaps the userspace base (0x2000000) and corrupts userspace process memory.

nodes.label: TCP Zero-Window Stall Fix
nodes.rationale: TCP stack sends unsolicited window-update ACK when app drains a throttled receive buffer; receive buffer grew 4KB→16KB. Dropped fresh-host TLS handshake from 5.5s→60ms and google.com load from ~20s→~1.1s.

nodes.label: OOM Killer and TLB Shootdown Fix
nodes.rationale: Heavy browser page triggered OOM. Fixed: freelist_pop validates nodes before deref, page-eviction issues cross-CPU TLB shootdown, OOM-killer SIGKILLs the demanding userspace task instead of returning ENOMEM.
nodes.norm_label: oom killer and tlb shootdown fix

nodes.label: Mesa VirGL b1nix Winsys (no libdrm)
nodes.rationale: b1nix has no DRM/GEM layer so the Mesa gallium virgl winsys maps struct virgl_winsys ops directly onto /dev/virtio-gpu ioctls. A b1nix res_id IS the host resource id; SUBMIT/TRANSFER are synchronous so fences are trivial.

nodes.label: b1nix Mesa VirGL Winsys Implementation
nodes.rationale: Upstream virgl_drm_winsys.c talks to Linux DRM via libdrm; b1nix has neither. The b1nix winsys maps virgl ops onto /dev/virtio-gpu ioctls. GEM handle maps 1:1 to b1nix res_id; PRIME/dma-buf/blob paths are dropped.

nodes.label: FPU State Not Flushed at exec/fork Bug Fix
nodes.rationale: exec arch_fpu_init_current reset live FPU but never flushed task's fpu_state buffer (kzalloc zero = FCW=0x0000). fork then copied zero buffer + fpu_initialized=1, so child restored unmasked FCW. TurboFan triggered #MF via nearbyint fldenv. Fix: flush clean FPU into save-area at exec; snapshot live FPU at fork.
nodes.norm_label: fpu state not flushed at exec/fork bug fix

nodes.label: Per-Thread ELF TLS Fix for V8 Worker Threads
nodes.rationale: pthread_create cloned WITHOUT CLONE_SETTLS; spawned threads got no per-thread .tdata/.tbss copy so V8 thread_local reads faulted (FS base=0). Added SYS_GET_TLS_INFO(161) and made pthread_create build a variant-II TLS block per thread mirroring the loader's main-thread layout.
nodes.norm_label: per-thread elf tls fix for v8 worker threads

nodes.label: user_jump.S FS Base Clobbered at Ring3 Entry Bug Fix
nodes.rationale: x86_user_jump did 'mov %ax,%fs' (user-data selector) on way to ring3; in 64-bit mode loading a segment selector ZEROES the base, wiping IA32_FS_BASE MSR the loader programmed. Fix: snapshot FS base (rdmsr 0xC0000100) before selector load and restore (wrmsr) after, stashing eax/edx/ecx (which alias argc/argv) in scratch registers.
nodes.norm_label: user_jump.s fs base clobbered at ring3 entry bug fix

nodes.label: SMP TLB Shootdown Deadlock in sys_mmap Fix
nodes.rationale: V8 large JIT cage/NORESERVE mmaps walked thousands of pages in sys_mmap page-mapping loops with no chance to take shootdown IPI; initiator on another CPU spun to 2^28 guard and panicked. Fix: call tlb_shootdown_poll() once per page in both sys_mmap loops.
nodes.norm_label: smp tlb shootdown deadlock in sys_mmap fix

nodes.label: V8 Pointer Compression with External Code Space Off
nodes.rationale: External code space base comes up ZERO on b1nix so JIT'd/builtin code pointers decompress to near-null. Fix: v8_enable_pointer_compression=true, v8_enable_external_code_space=false. Data cage was fine all along.
nodes.norm_label: v8 pointer compression with external code space off

nodes.label: linker-cxx.ld Missing .tdata/.tbss Sections Bug
nodes.rationale: linker-cxx.ld had no .tdata/.tbss rule so ld placed V8's COMDAT .tbss sections as orphans overlapping at one address. V8 thread_local vars for thread_id, g_current_isolate_, g_current_per_isolate_thread_data_ all collided at ti=0x18. Fix: add .tdata and .tbss rules so each thread_local gets a distinct PT_TLS offset.

nodes.label: PROT_NONE mmap Eager Frame Allocation Fix
nodes.rationale: PROT_NONE anonymous mmap allocated frames eagerly. V8 cage/DecommitPages churn drained and corrupted the PMM free list. Fix: PROT_NONE anonymous mmap uses the lazy (no-frame) path.
nodes.norm_label: prot_none mmap eager frame allocation fix

nodes.label: posix_memalign/aligned_alloc Stub Fix for V8
nodes.rationale: posix_memalign/aligned_alloc/memalign were stubs that ignored alignment (just malloc/16B). V8 needs Isolate page-aligned (AlignedAlloc(sizeof(Isolate), 4096)) for isolate_data_ 64-alignment. Rewrote with real over-aligned allocation using sentinel below payload so plain free() recovers it.

nodes.label: Dropping -lpthread/-lc/-lm in Autotools Wrapper
nodes.rationale: -lpthread/-lc/-lm/-lrt/-ldl/-lutil/-lcrypt/-lresolv/-lnsl are all provided by libb1nix.a (always whole-archived). Dropping them prevents ld 'unable to find -lX' errors when a port configured with --enable-threads emits -lpthread.
